Thursday. 9:15 AM. Sameer hands you a teal cap. Not a training cap. The real one. There's a number stitched on the back.
Everybody gets a speech when they get this. Mine was twenty minutes long. I'll give you three words. Bat like Kuttanad.
Put the cap on and say nothing.
Some moments don't need words.
"Nine times, Captain. Thank you for the tenth."
Say it.
Don't thank me. Score.
On the riverbank in Kuttanad, it's 2 PM, and nobody has gone to work. The temple has stopped ringing its bell so people can hear the commentary.
Forty-four overs gone. You came in at five, with the team wobbling. You've batted for an hour and a half. Sixty-two runs. Not one ball has been easy.
Now it's the last over. The scoreboard is very simple and very cruel.
12 off 6
Your World Cup debut. The fastest attack in the tournament. Your village is watching on a bedsheet. Twelve to win.
WORLD CUP WIN!
Four hundred people on a riverbank lose their minds.
SO CLOSE
The whole stadium stands for the new boy.
The last ball goes high over long-on and lands in a sea of teal and orange flags.
Before you even think about it, your hand goes to your collar.
In Kuttanad, a man in a checked shirt and a white wrap-around sarong falls off the roof of his own auto-rickshaw. He is fine. He will tell the story for the rest of his life.
Two short. Brennan's last ball is a perfect yorker. You dig it out and run, and it isn't enough. Seventy-one runs, on debut, in a losing team. And yet, when you walk off, the whole stadium stands.
On the way, your hand goes to your collar. A camera catches it.
Within an hour, the clip has twelve million views. "Who is he touching his collar for?" Everyone has a theory. A girlfriend. A god. A curse.
Twelve million. My phone has been ringing since the last ball. Everyone wants to know who the collar is for.
"For Shibu. My friend with the auto."
Tell the world.
"For everyone in Kuttanad watching on a bedsheet."
Tell the world, bigger.
"That's between me and the collar."
Keep the secret. Shibu will love it.
That's going to be the best headline I've written this year.

"BOARD INQUIRY: Reporter Diya Nair named in leak."
